title: Pricing companion products when the window is short
author: Editorial
excerpt: Short windows punish overthinking. Price companions to attach, not to maximize margin on day one.
body:
Companion pricing is attach-rate math, not premium-brand math. If the hero product is $48, your companion should feel like a painless yes — often 15–35% of hero price for physical, lower for digital.

Anchor to the ritual, not the BOM. Buyers pay for completion: "finish the set," "ship ready," "skip the hunt." Show the time saved, not the grams of material.

Use one visible price and one bundle. Decoy tiers waste cognitive load in a 72-hour window. If you need upsell, make it a post-purchase email, not a checkout fork.

Test price against speed: would you rather learn optimal margin or ship before the campaign ends? Makers who win short windows choose speed, then iterate on the next detection.
